description: ODC: the COMPLETE aggregate - two sources connected by JOIN, filter with implicit parameter, sort and group by with aggregations over BOTH sides of the join. Mirrors tests/jobs/aggregate-full.json of the O11 lane. This is how a real aggregate is built in the model, and the dump at the end shows the tree that the census counts: each IAliasedSource is born as an IAddSourceOperation; the IJoin, the IFilter and the ISort live inside the ICombineSourcesOperation, the stage that runs BEFORE the grouping (so the three cite the attributes by the alias of the source); the group by and the aggregated columns stay in the IGroupByOperation; and the filter that cites a parameter of the action makes an IImplicitParameter be born - the aggregate does not read variables from outside, it receives the value through a parameter of its own. ODC differences adapted here: the type of the aggregated column is called IAggregatedAttribute (in SS11 it is IAggregateAttribute) and both Count and Sum return Long Integer (in SS11, Integer); only List.Length remains Integer.

expectedMessages.why: ODC: an app (CrossDevice) does not expose a public server action (the live Studio gives an error); the action stays private and without a consumer in this proof job

ops.name: WfGetOrdersByCustomer
ops._why: OWN name, not the default name of the Studio (GetWfAggOrders): on receiving a filter the platform would rename the aggregate by itself and all the expressions that cite it would break
first source = first IAddSourceOperation of the aggregate
second source: it is the existence of TWO that makes the join possible
the join lives in the ICombineSourcesOperation, the stage that runs after adding the sources and before the group by
the condition cites both sides by the source ALIAS, which by default is the name of the entity

the filter cites MinTotal, a parameter of the ACTION: the aggregate does not read variables from outside, so the platform creates an IImplicitParameter inside it and links it to the parameter. The dump at the end proves this

the dump at the end shows that the sort lives in the ICombineSourcesOperation, that is, it runs BEFORE the group by: that is why it cites the attribute by the alias of the source (WfAggOrder.CustomerName) and not the name of the grouped column

ops.name: QtySum
ops._why: aggregation over the RIGHT side of the join: it is the proof that the join really entered the query, and not just the drawing
WITH group by the row is an anonymous structure: the column is read directly, WITHOUT the alias WfAggOrder.
how many grouped ROWS came back (one per customer), not how many orders
reads back the join: the two sides, the type and the condition
proves the type of the Count in ODC: Long Integer
proves the whole tree of the aggregate: two sources, join, filter, the IImplicitParameter that the filter created, sort, group by and the two aggregated columns
the attribute of the right side is consumed by the Sum aggregation: the join is not decoration
